Have you looked at a modern airplane? Have you followed from year to year the evolution of its lines? Have you ever thought, not only about the airplane but about whatever man builds, that all of man's industrial efforts, all his computations and calculations, all the nights spent over working draughts and blueprints, invariably culminate in the production of a thing whose sole and guiding principle is the ultimate principle of simplicity?

It is as if there were a natural law which ordained that to achieve this end, to refine the curve of a piece of furniture, or a ship's keel, or the fuselage of an airplane, until gradually it partakes of the elementary purity of the curve of a human breast or shoulder, there must be the experimentation of several generations of craftsmen. In anything at all, perfection is finally attained not when there is no longer anything to add, but when there is no longer anything to take away, when a body has been stripped down to its nakedness.
Antoine de Saint-Exupéry on the simplicity of good design

I usually don't watch movies because I can't really get invested in the story or characters in such a short amount of time. KnK doesn't have this problem so for me it's a nice change of pace compared to 12/24 episode series. I didn't know anything about KnK beforehand except that the story was non-linear.

Episode 1 was darker than I'd expected. It felt even darker than episode 2 and 3, but maybe that's because I wasn't used to the setting yet. My least favorite episode up until now, mostly because I still don't have any idea what happened. It has some references to the third episode: they talk about a bridge that has collapsed and show that Shiki has an artificial arm.

Episode 2 was pretty cool. It showed the entire backstory between Shiki and Kokutou, but it didn't really explain much. Shiki expresses murderous intent, but they don't directly show her killing people like they did with Fujino in episode 3. Kokutou also doesn't seem to believe that Shiki is capable of killing people. I hope we get to see why she ended up in the hospital soon and if something happened between Shiki and the other woman in the hospital from episode one.

Episode 3 is my favorite so far. It showed more of Shiki and explained some of the unresolved questions from episode 2. Fujino's story about being a person without pain was interesting as well. I wonder if Shiki has any special magical powers like Fujino. In episode 1 we saw her jumping to a rooftop from a great height and in episode 3 she also made a big jump off the bridge. We also saw she has (had?) a split personality, I wonder if she's had that from when she was born or if that's a consequence of her powers. Interestingly Fujino also ends up being brought to the hospital.

I love the music, Yuki Kajiura and Kalafina are awesome. The animation is great as well, as expected from ufotable.
